title: AIT Bangkok GIIP 2026 — 15 Days of Innovation | Gautam Kumar Maurya
description: A photo-backed field journal of the Global Innovation Internship Program (GIIP 2026) at the Asian Institute of Technology, Bangkok: 15 days, 12 learning domains, 8 faculty mentors and the BusSetu real-time transit capstone, 1–15 June 2026.

programme.name: Global Innovation Internship Program (GIIP) 2026
programme.location: AIT Conference Center, Pathum Thani, Bangkok, Thailand
instructors: Dr. Nitin Tripathi (Director, Special Degree Programs)
Dr. Chutiporn Anutariya (Associate Professor, Computer Science & Information Management)
programme.outcome: Certificate of completion at the AIT closing ceremony, plus a team capstone (BusSetu) defended before an AIT faculty panel.

capstone.name: BusSetu
capstone.summary: A real-time public-transport platform that blends GTFS schedules with GPS telemetry to project bus arrival times on a vector map.
capstone.role: Led the system architecture and low-latency map layer; presented the working prototype to the AIT panel.

days.label: Mon 01 Jun 2026
days.title: Landfall in Bangkok, then north to AIT
days.summary: Landed at Suvarnabhumi in the late morning and took the delegation transfer north to Pathum Thani. The first shock was scale: AIT's campus is a green research town, not a city block. Check-in at the AIT Conference Center, a quick tour, then a cohort dinner that made the next fortnight feel real.
notes: Suvarnabhumi → AIT campus transfer with the delegation.
Campus orientation, conference-center check-in and welcome dinner.
days.photoCaption: The GIIP 2026 cohort outside AIT's academic building

days.label: Tue 02 Jun 2026
days.title: Induction, safety and the shape of the fortnight
days.summary: The formal start. Dr. Nitin Tripathi welcomed the cohort on behalf of AIT's Special Degree Programs office, followed by a safety and lab-access briefing. We mapped deliverables against the calendar, met the teaching teams and split into project groups.
notes: Welcome address and programme expectations from the SDP directorate.
Lab access, research ethics and cohort assignments.
days.photoCaption: Opening session in the AIT auditorium

days.label: Wed 03 Jun 2026
days.title: AI and the discipline of a good prompt
days.summary: An intensive day on large-language-model behaviour: system instructions, structured output, context limits and the difference between a demo and something you can ship. Most of the value was in the constraints — getting a model to return clean JSON, then testing it against edge cases.
notes: System vs user instructions, chain-of-thought and output schemas.
Context-window budgeting and token-management strategies.
days.photoCaption: A teaching-room session during the AI module

days.label: Thu 04 Jun 2026
days.title: Ubiquitous GIS: the campus becomes a dataset
days.summary: Field survey day. We built collection forms in EpiCollect5, walked the campus capturing spatial points, then pulled the export into QGIS. The lesson was less about software than integrity: a coordinate is only useful if you know how it was captured.
notes: Mobile form design and spatial point capture with EpiCollect5.
First QGIS layer, coordinate checks and attribute cleanup.
days.photoCaption: A field walk across the AIT campus

days.label: Fri 05 Jun 2026
days.title: EDA: cleaning the survey before trusting it
days.summary: Python, Pandas and a hundred-plus spatial points. We joined the survey export to the campus layers, checked missing values, fixed inconsistent categories and looked for the first honest patterns. Most of the day was spent on data quality — which is the point.
notes: Pandas cleaning, joins and descriptive statistics on the survey set.
Plotting spatial distributions before making any claims.
days.photoCaption: A workstation session in an AIT computer lab

days.label: Sat 06 Jun 2026
days.title: IoT, sensors and the noise of the real world
days.summary: From software to solder. The sensor benches covered microcontrollers, wiring, sampling and serial telemetry. Getting a stable reading was easy; getting a stable reading for an hour was the actual exercise. This was the day the programme's hardware thread became concrete.
notes: Microcontroller setup, sensor wiring and serial output.
Reading noise, sampling rate and basic calibration.

days.label: Sun 07 Jun 2026
days.title: KMITL: six-axis arms and trajectory thinking
days.summary: A visit to King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang (KMITL) for its robotics and automation work. Seeing six-axis arms move made kinematic constraints and path planning tangible — and made the gap between a scripted demo and a reliable cell obvious.
notes: Robotic arm kinematics and trajectory planning, demonstrated on six-axis hardware.
Discussion of automation workflows and lab-to-industry translation.

days.label: Mon 08 Jun 2026
days.title: Corporate communication: the pitch is the product
days.summary: A shift from technical to human. The corporate-communication module covered executive pitch structure, cross-cultural framing and handling hard questions without losing the thread. We rehearsed short pitches in front of the room — useful preparation for the defence at the end of the fortnight.
notes: Pitch structure for technical work: problem, evidence, demo, ask.
Cross-cultural communication and live question handling.
days.photoCaption: A workshop led from the front of the room

days.label: Tue 09 Jun 2026
days.title: A science museum, a city and a cultural evening
days.summary: A day in Bangkok. We visited the National Science Museum and spent the evening with the cohort. The value was context: Thailand's investment in science communication, its design language and the way the city organises public space. It made the fortnight feel less like a bubble.
notes: National Science Museum and Bangkok cultural immersion.
Cohort evening and informal exchange with international peers.
days.photoCaption: A cultural performance during the Bangkok immersion

days.label: Wed 10 Jun 2026
days.title: Design thinking, and the birth of BusSetu
days.summary: Problem framing day. We mapped rider journeys, argued about scope and deliberately narrowed the first version: scheduled routes, live vehicle position, projected arrival. No payments, no accounts, no marketplace. The constraint made the next sprint possible.
notes: Rider interviews and a journey map of the daily wait.
Scope decision: GTFS schedules + GPS telemetry + a map.
days.photoCaption: Framing the BusSetu problem on paper

days.label: Thu 11 Jun 2026
days.title: Power BI: making the numbers legible
days.summary: A dashboard day. We built a small model, wrote DAX measures and designed for an executive reader who has ninety seconds. The recurring lesson: a chart is an argument, not decoration. Every visual had to answer a specific question.
notes: Data model and relationship design in Power BI.
DAX measures and a dashboard narrative for non-specialists.
days.photoCaption: An analytics workshop in an AIT teaching room

days.label: Fri 12 Jun 2026
days.title: Agentic AI: workflows that take a step
days.summary: The final teaching block. Tool calling, task decomposition and memory patterns — how an agent chains steps instead of answering once. Most of the discussion was about guardrails: what the system may do, when it must stop and how a human stays in the loop.
notes: Tool invocation, decomposition and short-term memory in agent loops.
Guardrails, observability and human checkpoints.
days.photoCaption: A full-cohort session on agentic workflows

days.label: Sat 13 Jun 2026
days.title: Build sprint: schedules in, a live map out
days.summary: The build day. We parsed GTFS schedules, stitched in GPS telemetry and pushed arrival projections onto a vector map. I owned the architecture and the low-latency map layer; the team owned the surrounding flow. By evening the prototype was deployed on Vercel and holding under a demo load.
notes: GTFS parser, GPS telemetry and Google Maps API integration.
Latency work on the map layer, then a Vercel deploy.

days.label: Sun 14 Jun 2026
days.title: The defence: architecture, latency, questions
days.summary: Presentation day. We walked the AIT faculty panel through the rider problem, the data pipeline and a live demo, then took questions on accuracy, failure modes and what we would build next. The prototype held. The panel's feedback was direct and the project closed with a top commendation.
notes: Architecture walkthrough, live demo and measured outcomes.
Panel Q&A on ETA accuracy, latency and operational limits.
days.photoCaption: Presentation day on the AIT stage

days.label: Mon 15 Jun 2026
days.title: Certificates, photographs, and the flight home
days.summary: The closing ceremony. Certificates were presented, the cohort took its last set of photographs and we swapped contacts over a farewell dinner. Then the airport run and a night flight back to India — fifteen days that reorganised how I think about building software.
notes: GIIP 2026 certificate presentation and cohort photographs.
Farewell dinner, then the return flight to India.

faq.a: GIIP 2026 is the Global Innovation Internship Program run at the Asian Institute of Technology in Thailand. The 15-day edition ran from 1 to 15 June 2026, covering AI, GIS, IoT, robotics and agentic workflows, and closed with a team capstone.

faq.q: Where and when did it take place?
faq.a: At the Asian Institute of Technology campus in Pathum Thani, north of central Bangkok, from 1 to 15 June 2026. Sessions used AIT teaching rooms and labs, with a KMITL visit and a cultural day in Bangkok.

faq.q: What did you build during the fellowship?
faq.a: BusSetu, a real-time public transport platform that combines GTFS schedules with GPS telemetry to project bus arrivals on a vector map. I led the architecture and map layer and presented the prototype to the AIT faculty panel.

faq.q: Was this an internship, a course or a fellowship?
faq.a: It ran as a structured international innovation programme: taught modules, lab and field work, a team capstone and a certificate at the closing ceremony. AIT's Special Degree Programs office hosted the cohort.

faq.q: How can I verify the programme or the certificate?
faq.a: The programme is recorded on the roles and responsibilities ledger and in the achievements dossier, with dates and context. The certificate was presented at the AIT closing ceremony, and the BusSetu prototype remains live.

faq.q: What was the most useful part of the 15 days?
faq.a: The forced loop from field data to a working product: collect spatial data, clean it, model it, then defend a live interface built on top of it. The BusSetu sprint turned the whole fortnight into one testable system.
